title: Algebraic numbers and real closed fields
text: Arithmetic stays exact:
code: r <- z3_real(ctx, "r") s <- z3_solver(ctx) z3_add(s, r^2 == 2, r > 0) z3_check(s) #> [1] "sat" root2 <- z3_eval(z3_model(s), r) root2 #> <z3_expr Real> (root-obj (+ (^ x 2) (- 2)) 2) z3_decimal(root2, 40) #> [1] "1.4142135623730950488016887242096980785696?" z3_algebraic_poly(root2) #> $coefficients #> $coefficients[[1]] #> <z3_expr Real> (- 2.0) #>  #> $coefficients[[2]] #> <z3_expr Real> 0.0 #>  #> $coefficients[[3]] #> <z3_expr Real> 1.0 #>  #>  #> $index #> [1] 2 z3_algebraic("*", root2, root2) #> <z3_expr Real> 2.0 z3_algebraic("+", root2, 1) #> <z3_expr Real> (root-obj (+ (^ x 2) (* (- 2) x) (- 1)) 2) z3_algebraic("<", root2, z3_real_val(ctx, "1.4142136")) #> [1] TRUE z3_algebraic_power(root2, 6) #> <z3_expr Real> 8.0 cbrt5 <- z3_algebraic_root(z3_real_val(ctx, 5), 3) z3_algebraic_power(cbrt5, 3) #> <z3_expr Real> 5.0 z3_algebraic_sign(z3_algebraic("-", cbrt5, root2)) #> [1] 1

title: Arrays, sets and lambdas
text: Z3 array maps every value index sort value element sort. length: arrays model memory, tables functions. Constant arrays give every index value:
code: a <- z3_array(ctx, "a", I, I) i <- z3_int(ctx, "i") j <- z3_int(ctx, "j") s <- z3_solver(ctx) # Reading back what was written always succeeds... z3_add(s, z3_select(z3_store(a, i, 42), i) != 42) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat" # ...and writing at i never changes another index s <- z3_solver(ctx) z3_add(s, i != j, z3_select(z3_store(a, i, 42), j) != z3_select(a, j)) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat" zeros <- z3_const_array(I, 0) z3_simplify(z3_select(z3_store(zeros, 3, 7), 3)) #> <z3_expr Int> 7

title: Arrays, sets and lambdas
text: Swapping two elements twice restores array, every array every pair indices:
code: swap <- function(arr, p, q) {   vp <- z3_select(arr, p)   vq <- z3_select(arr, q)   z3_store(z3_store(arr, p, vq), q, vp) } s <- z3_solver(ctx) k <- z3_int(ctx, "k") z3_add(s, z3_select(swap(swap(a, i, j), i, j), k) != z3_select(a, k)) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat"

title: Bit-vectors: machine integers and program verification
text: Comparison, division right shift depend bits read, z3r provides versions overload < / bit-vectors: &, | ! bitwise bit-vectors; z3_bvxor(), z3_bvshl(), rotations, z3_concat(), z3_extract() extensions complete set:
code: x <- z3_bv(ctx, "x", 8) x < 3 #> Error: #> ! '<' is not defined for bit-vectors because signed and unsigned semantics differ; use z3_bvult(), z3_bvslt(), z3_bvudiv(), z3_bvsdiv() and related functions val <- function(e) z3_value(z3_simplify(e)) c(unsigned = val(z3_bvult(b8(200), b8(100))), signed = val(z3_bvslt(b8(200), b8(100)))) #> unsigned   signed  #>    FALSE     TRUE c(udiv = val(z3_bvudiv(b8(200), b8(3))), sdiv = z3_value(z3_simplify(z3_bvsdiv(b8(200), b8(3))), signed = TRUE)) #> udiv sdiv  #>   66  -18 c(lshr = val(z3_bvlshr(b8(0x80), b8(7))), ashr = val(z3_bvashr(b8(0x80), b8(7)))) #> lshr ashr  #>    1  255 val(b8(0xF0) & b8(0x3C)) #> [1] 48 val(z3_extract(b8(0xAB), 7, 4)) #> [1] 10 val(z3_concat(z3_bv_val(ctx, 0xA, 4), z3_bv_val(ctx, 0xB, 4))) #> [1] 171 val(z3_sign_ext(b8(0x80), 8)) #> [1] 65408 val(z3_rotate_left(b8(0x81), 1)) #> [1] 3

title: Bit-vectors: machine integers and program verification
text: z3_bvadd_no_overflow() friends state operation overflow. Asking counterexample “overflow” finds inputs break computation:
code: a <- z3_bv(ctx, "a", 32) b <- z3_bv(ctx, "b", 32) s <- z3_solver(ctx) # The classic midpoint bug: (a + b) / 2 overflows for large indices z3_add(s, z3_bvsge(a, 0), z3_bvsge(b, 0), !z3_bvadd_no_overflow(a, b, signed = TRUE)) z3_check(s) #> [1] "sat" m <- z3_model(s) c(a = z3_value(z3_eval(m, a)), b = z3_value(z3_eval(m, b))) #>          a          b  #> 2147418111 1073807364 # The fix a + (b - a) / 2 never overflows when 0 <= a <= b s <- z3_solver(ctx) z3_add(s, z3_bvsge(a, 0), z3_bvsle(a, b),        !z3_bvadd_no_overflow(a, z3_bvsdiv(b - a, z3_bv_val(ctx, 2, 32)), signed = TRUE)) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat"

title: Bit-vectors: machine integers and program verification
text: branch-free absolute value (x ^ (x >> 31)) - (x >> 31) equals obvious definition 2^32 inputs: “x power two” x & (x - 1) == 0: Counting bits well-known parallel trick, checked direct sum bits:
code: v <- z3_bv(ctx, "v", 32) m <- z3_bvashr(v, 31) s <- z3_solver(ctx) z3_add(s, z3_bvxor(v, m) - m != z3_ite(z3_bvslt(v, 0), -v, v)) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat" x <- z3_bv(ctx, "x", 16) s <- z3_solver(ctx) is_pow2 <- z3_or(lapply(0:15, function(k) x == 2^k)) z3_add(s, x != 0, ((x & (x - 1)) == 0) != is_pow2) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat" x <- z3_bv(ctx, "x", 8) k <- function(v) z3_bv_val(ctx, v, 8) c1 <- x - (z3_bvlshr(x, k(1)) & k(0x55)) c2 <- (c1 & k(0x33)) + (z3_bvlshr(c1, k(2)) & k(0x33)) c3 <- (c2 + z3_bvlshr(c2, k(4))) & k(0x0F) naive <- z3_sum(lapply(0:7, function(i) z3_zero_ext(z3_extract(x, i, i), 7))) s <- z3_solver(ctx) z3_add(s, c3 != naive) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat"

code: p <- z3_bools(ctx, paste0("p", 1:6)) s <- z3_solver(ctx)  true_terms <- list()   # terms currently assigned TRUE marks <- integer()     # length of true_terms at each push  z3_propagator(s,   push = function(cb) marks <<- c(marks, length(true_terms)),   pop = function(cb, n) {     keep <- marks[length(marks) - n + 1]     true_terms <<- true_terms[seq_len(keep)]     marks <<- marks[seq_len(length(marks) - n)]   },   fixed = function(cb, term, value) {     if (isTRUE(z3_value(value))) {       true_terms[[length(true_terms) + 1]] <<- term       if (length(true_terms) > 2) z3_propagate_conflict(cb, true_terms)     }   }) for (v in p) z3_propagate_register(s, v) z3_add(s, z3_or(p[1:3]), z3_or(p[4:6])) z3_check(s) #> [1] "sat" unlist(z3_model_values(z3_model(s))) #>    p2    p1    p3    p4    p6    p5  #> FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE z3_add(s, p$p1, p$p2, p$p4) z3_check(s) #> [1] "unsat"
